questions.q: Two particles of equal mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> move in a circle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The speed of each particle will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let speed of both the particles be v.

Then, gravitational force between the particles will provide the required centripetal force.

Therefore,

Gmm2r2=mv2r

⇒v=Gm4r

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi></math>. If the diameter of earth reduces to half of its original value and mass remains constant, then acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity is related to the mass and the radius of the Earth by the formula:

g=GMR2⇒g∝1R2   ...1

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

g2 g1=R12R22=R12R122=4⇒g2=4g

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is projected with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></math> in vertically upward direction from the surface of the earth into space. It is given that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></math> is escape velocity and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. If air resistance is considered to the negligible, then the maximum height from the centre of earth, to which the body can go, will be (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> : radius of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Escape velocity is given by, ve=2GMeRe

If the body goes to the height h from the surface of the earth, using mechanical energy conservation,

⇒12mλ2GMeRe2-GMemRe=-GMemRe+h

⇒λ2GMemRe-GMemRe=-GMemRe+h

⇒Re+h=Re1-λ2

questions.q: If a satellite orbiting the Earth is 9 times closer to the Earth than the Moon, what is the time period of rotation of the satellite? Given rotational time period of Moon $=27$ days and gravitational attraction between the satellite and the moon is neglected.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}^2 \propto \mathrm{R}^3 \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{s}}}\right)^2=\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R} / 9}\right)^3 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{s}}}=(3)^3 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{s}}=\left(\frac{27}{27}\right)=1 \text { day }\end{aligned}$

=∫0RKr24πr2dr

It is again equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> at a depth <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> below the surface the earth. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>R</mi></mfrac></mfenced></math> equals:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that

gn=gd

GM(R+h)2=GMR3(R-d)

GM(R+R/2)2=GMR3(R-d)

4GM9R2=GMR21-dR

49=1-dR

questions.q: The gravitational potential at a point above the surface of earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the acceleration due to gravity at that point is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Assume that the mean radius of earth to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math>. The height of this point above the earth's surface is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Gravitational potential at a distance r from the centre of the earth is given by, V=-GMr.

Therefore, we can write

-GMERE+h=-5.12×107    …i

also acceleration due to gravity at that point will be

GMERE+h2=6.4    …ii

By (i) and (ii), we get

-GMERE+hGMERE+h2=5.12×1076.4

⇒RE+h=80×105 m=8000 km⇒h=8000 km-6400 km=1600 km

questions.q: A satellite is launched into a circular orbit of radius ' R ' around the earth. A second satellite is launched into an orbit of radius 1.03 R . The time period of revolution of the second satellite is larger than the first one approximately by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $T_1 \propto(R)^{3 / 2}$ and $T_2 \propto(1.03 R)^{3 / 2}\Rightarrow \quad T_2=(1.03 R)^{3 / 2} \cdot T_1 \approx 1.045 T_1$ So $T_2$ will larger by $4.5 \%$ w.r.t. $T_1$.

questions.q: The masses and radii of the earth and moon are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> respectively. Their centres are at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> apart. Find the minimum escape velocity for a particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math>  to be projected from the middle of these two masses :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
On conserving mechanical energy. The initial total energy is equal to final total energy, ⇒-GM1r2+GM2r2m+12mve2=0
⇒ve=4GM1+M2r.

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is the gravitational potential due to sphere of uniform density on its surface, then its value at the centre of sphere will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnitude of gravitational potential of a solid sphere at a distance r from the centre is 

V=-GM2R3(3R2-r2)

At r=R, V=-GMR.

At r=0, V'=-GM2R3(3R2)=-3GM2R

Clearly, V'=3V2.

questions.q: Four identical particles of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> are kept at the four corners of a square. If the gravitational force exerted on one of the masses by the other masses is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>32</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mfrac><mrow><mi>G</mi><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>, the length of the sides of the square is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resultant force, Fnet=2F+F', where

F=Gm2a2 and F'=Gm22a2

Therefore, Fnet=2Gm2a2+Gm22a2

Comparing with the expression given in the question, we get

22+132Gm2L2=Gm2a222+12

⇒a=4L

questions.q:
A body weighs 49 N on a spring balance at the north pole. What will be its weight recorded on the same weighing machine, if it is shifted to the equator?

[Use g=GMR2=9.8 m s-2 and radius of earth, R=6400 km.]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Weight of pole =mg=49 N

At equator due to rotation =ge=g-Rω2

so W=mge=mg-Rω2

∴  WP>We Wp=49 N

So, We=48.83 N. We<49 N

options: Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true and $\mathrm{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
(4) Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true but $\mathrm{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{Gm}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)=\mathrm{mgR}$
Assertion wrong
at $\infty$
$\mathrm{U}=0$

questions.solution:
From Kepler's Third Law(The Law of Periods), we know

T2∝R3 ⇒T22T12=R2R13=3RR3

Therefore, T2=27T1

=5.19×7≈36 hours

questions.q: Four identical particles of mass M are located at the corners of a square of side ‘a’ . What should be their speed if each of them revolves under the influence of other’s gravitational field in a circular orbit circumscribing the square?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Gravitational force on each mass 'M'
=2GM2a2+GM22a2=2+12GM2a2
This force will provide required centripetal force
2+12GM2a2=Mv2(a/2)
v=1+122GMa=1.16GMa

questions.q: Acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is ' $g$ '. If the diameter of earth is reduced to one third of its original value and mass remains unchanged, then the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is $\ldots\ldots$ g.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\because$ acceleration due to gravity on surface is given by
$\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^2}$

Now since diameter is reduced to $1 / 3^{\text {rd }}$, radius also reduces to $1 / 3^{\text {rd }}$, keeping mass constant
New value of acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is
$\mathrm{g}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{3}\right)^2}=9 \frac{\mathrm{GMe}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^2}=9 \mathrm{~g}$

gA=GMrR3

gC=GMR+R22
gA=gC

rR3=194R2⇒r=4R9

so OA=4R9; AB=R-r=5R9

OA:AB=4:5

questions.q: Two planets, $A$ and $B$ are orbiting a common star in circular orbits of radii $R_A$ and $R_B$, respectively, with $R_B=2 R_A$. The planet $B$ is $4 \sqrt{2}$ times more massive than planet $A$. The ratio $\left(\frac{L_B}{L_A}\right)$ of angular momentum $\left(L_B\right)$ of planet $B$ to that of planet $A\left(L_A\right)$ is closest to integer ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{mv}_0 \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{m} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}}} \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{m} \sqrt{\mathrm{GMR}}$
here M is mass of star
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{A}}} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}} \\
& =4 \sqrt{2} \sqrt{\frac{2}{1}} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{A}}}=8
\end{aligned}$
